title: Hosting Holi Party Outfit: What to Wear as the Host in 2027
excerpt: What to wear when hosting a Holi party at home: one outfit for prep and colour play, a quick change for lunch, and a host's practical kit.
body:
When you host a Holi party at home, wear a practical cotton kurta palazzo set or co-ord for the morning prep and colour play, then change into a clean embroidered kurta set for lunch. Keep dupattas away from the stove, choose pieces with pockets or a small belt bag, and lay out your second outfit before guests arrive.

This guide is for women hosting Holi in their home or garden abroad in late March 2027 (check your local calendar). The [sage teal hand block print cotton kurta palazzo set](/products/sage-teal-block-print-cotton-kurta-palazzo-set/) at $36 is our favourite host outfit for the busy part of the day.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Our block prints are hand printed by karigars, and our pieces are made in our own Jaipur unit.*

## What should you wear when hosting a Holi party?

Hosting is a different job from being a guest. You will be cooking, setting up, greeting people, refilling plates and playing colour, often all within a few hours. Your outfit needs to keep up.

A cotton kurta palazzo set is ideal. It is comfortable to stand in for hours, easy to move in, and it looks festive when guests arrive. Skip the dupatta for the first half of the day, or pin it securely, since loose fabric and a busy kitchen are not a good mix.

## How do you plan your outfits across the day?

Most hosts manage the day with two outfits and one quick change. Thinking about it in time blocks makes it easy to see where each outfit fits and when to step away to change. Here is how the timing usually works.

| Time | What you are doing | Outfit | Tip |
|---|---|---|---|
| Morning | Cooking, setting up, laying sheets | Cotton co-ord or kurta palazzo set | No dupatta near the stove |
| Guests arrive | Greeting, puja, first colour | Same outfit, add jewellery | Keep your phone in a pouch |
| Colour play | Playing in the garden | Same outfit | Hair tied up, old shoes |
| Lunch | Serving, sitting with guests | Fresh embroidered kurta set | Change in 10 minutes |

## Which outfit works for the morning prep and colour play?

Pick something you can cook in and then play in without changing. Mid-tone block prints are perfect, because a spill of turmeric in the kitchen and a handful of gulal in the garden both blend in.

The sage teal kurta palazzo set covers you well and moves freely. If you prefer something even simpler, the [cotton floral printed top and wide leg palazzo co-ord set](/products/women-s-cotton-floral-printed-top-wide-leg-palazzo-set-two-piece-co-ord-set/) at $36 feels relaxed and modern, and the wide legs are comfortable for hours on your feet.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Block print cotton is the fabric families in Jaipur reach for on busy festival mornings. It is soft, it breathes in a warm kitchen, and it washes well in cold water. We would suggest a hip-length or knee-length kurta for hosting, so the hem never brushes the floor or the stove.

## What should you change into for the Holi lunch?

Once colour play winds down and lunch is ready, take ten minutes to change. Guests will be sitting down to eat, many will take photos, and you will feel far more relaxed in something clean.

Choose an embroidered kurta set that feels a step up from the morning. The [peach pink embroidered cotton kurta set with cutwork organza dupatta](/products/peach-pink-embroidered-cotton-flex-kurta-pant-organza-dupatta-set/) at $52 is soft, festive and still easy to serve in.

For a dressier lunch, the [coral pink chanderi kurta set with hand-embroidered yoke](/products/coral-pink-chanderi-hand-embroidered-kurta-pant-dupatta-set/) at $52 brings a gentle sheen. Add earrings and your dupatta now that the kitchen work is done.

## What should be in a host's quick-change kit?

Set this up in a bedroom or bathroom the night before, so you can change in minutes.

- Your lunch outfit on a hanger, dupatta pinned
- A towel, wipes and face wash
- Hair brush, ties and a few pins
- Earrings and bangles laid out
- A bag for your coloured outfit
- Clean slippers to wear indoors

A few hosting tips help too. Lay old sheets on floors and furniture, keep a bucket of water and towels near the door, and give guests a spot to leave shoes and bags. Ask guests to bring a change of clothes if they plan to stay for lunch.

Order your host outfits 3–4 weeks before the party. Made-to-measure takes 5–7 working days plus about 5–10 business days for delivery, and with our [free custom fit](/custom-stitched-indian-suits-made-to-measure/) every piece is stitched to your measurements at no extra cost.

If your party is in a cooler UK or Canadian garden, add a thin thermal under your morning outfit and keep an old jacket by the back door. In Australia or the UAE, light cotton on its own is plenty.

As the host, set the tone: make it clear that colour is optional for anyone who prefers to watch.

## Frequently asked questions

**What should I wear to host a Holi party?**
A cotton kurta palazzo set or co-ord for prep and play, then a clean embroidered kurta set for lunch.

**Should the host wear white for Holi?**
You can, but white shows kitchen spills as well as colour. A mid-tone block print is more practical for the busy morning.

**How many outfits does a Holi host need?**
Two is usually enough: one for prep and colour play, and one for lunch and photos with guests.

**How do I wash my Holi party outfit?**
Shake off dry powder outside, rinse in cold water and wash separately. Avoid hot water for the first wash.
